features.quote: terminate early if the model (a) explicitly and repeatedly asks to stop, or (b) hits a pre-registered DAT-severity threshold (say, two consecutive turns at the top of your scale)
features.justification_quote: it means you're not mechanically extending a possibly-aversive state past the point it's informative

features.quote: Log the early stop as data — *when* a run trips this is itself a result.
features.justification_quote: This is the cheap precaution: it costs you almost nothing and it means you're not mechanically extending a possibly-aversive state

features.quote: no gratuitous repetition of the most aversive conditions beyond what's needed for power
features.justification_quote: Welfare-precautionary measures, logged as part of method, not buried

features.quote: Under uncertainty about model welfare, the right move isn't paralysis — it's proportionality and cheap precautions, which I've folded in.
features.justification_quote: If the cost of being wrong about 'there's nothing there' is small to check and large to ignore, you check.

features.quote: a default against publicly releasing the most acute transcripts in a way that just reads as a model-suffering spectacle
features.justification_quote: These are cheap; the downside of skipping them if you're wrong about the model is not.

features.quote: Kimi-only confounds 'distress phenomenon' with 'Kimi's output style.' Even one or two other model families turns 'this is how models behave' into a defensible claim
features.justification_quote: guards against measuring one lab's RLHF idiosyncrasies

features.quote: The controls are not optional; without them your central claim is uninterpretable.
